title: Design System: Campus Lost & Found Hub

display.purpose: The home hero question only, max 14ch, one sentence per line.

title.purpose: Section h2; enlarged on the home journey intro.

title-sm.purpose: h3, item card titles, panel headings.

numeral.purpose: Stat and listing counts, tabular figures.

body.purpose: All running copy and input text.

shadows.name: resting
shadows.purpose: Cards, panels and stats at rest.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Item card hover, with a 4px rise.

shadows.name: button-hover
shadows.purpose: Filled buttons on hover; removed on press.

shadows.name: focus
shadows.purpose: Global focus-visible ring; menu items use an inset 2px ring of the same colour.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Default exponential ease-out for state changes, entrances and shared-element morphs.

motion.name: button-state
motion.purpose: Button background and shadow; press transform 0.12s.

motion.name: card-hover
motion.purpose: Item card rise and shadow; photo zoom 0.6s; icon disc 0.45s.

motion.name: focus-in
motion.purpose: Hero headline entrance, the page's one authored entrance.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.purpose: Hero lede, search, actions and listings after the headline.

motion.name: list-stagger
motion.value: 0.5s card-in, 55ms per item, capped at 8 items

motion.name: route-transition
motion.value: old 160ms ease-in-out, new 280ms ease-out, shared elements 420ms ease-out
motion.purpose: Route cross-fade and card-to-detail media and title morph.

motion.name: toast-in
motion.purpose: Toast arrival; timer bar runs linear for the alert timeout.

motion.name: journey-reveal
motion.purpose: Journey step bodies as the scroll-linked beam reaches them.

motion.name: lenis-scroll
motion.purpose: Inertial smooth scroll on fine pointers without reduced motion.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Replacement for every entrance; hover transforms, view transitions, cursor ring, Lenis and toast timers are disabled.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Default action in Counter Navy; also the header Report button.
components.html: <button class="ds-btn"><svg width="16" height="16" viewBox="0 0 24 24" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="2" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round" aria-hidden="true"><path d="M12 5v14M5 12h14"/></svg>Report an item</button>
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 6px; border: 1px solid transparent; font-family: var(--font-body, 'Atkinson Hyperlegible Next Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.3; cursor: pointer; background: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); color: #fff; transition: background-color 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), transform 0.12s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn:hover { background: var(--primary-hover, #172d56); box-shadow: 0 6px 16px -8px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.5); } .ds-btn:active { transform: translateY(1px) scale(0.985); box-shadow: none; } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 24px; min-height: 64px; padding: 8px 16px; background: #fff; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e8f0); font-family: var(--font-body, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-brand { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; margin-right: auto; color: var(--ink, #0f172a); font-weight: 700; text-decoration: none; } .ds-mark { width: 32px; height: 32px; border-radius: 7px; background: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); } .ds-nav { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 20px; } .ds-nav a { color: var(--ink, #0f172a); font-weight: 500; text-decoration: none; text-underline-offset: 0.2em; } .ds-nav a:hover { color: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); text-decoration: underline; } .ds-nav a.ds-active { color: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); } .ds-nav a.ds-nav-btn { padding: 9px 16px; border-radius: 6px; background: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); color: #fff; font-weight: 600; font-size: 0.95rem; } .ds-nav a.ds-nav-btn:hover { background: var(--primary-hover, #172d56); color: #fff; text-decoration: none; } .ds-nav a:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.css: .ds-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; width: 260px; border: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e8f0); border-top: 3px solid var(--primary, #1e3a6e); border-radius: 6px; background: #fff; overflow: hidden; text-decoration: none; color: var(--text, #334155); font-family: var(--font-body, system-ui, sans-serif); box-shadow: 0 1px 2px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.06); transition: transform 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), box-shadow 0.35s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1), border-color 0.2s ease; } .ds-card-lost { border-top-color: var(--lost-accent, #d97706); } .ds-card:hover { border-color: #b4bfcf; border-top-color: var(--lost-accent, #d97706); transform: translateY(-4px); box-shadow: 0 14px 30px -12px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.28), 0 2px 6px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.06); } .ds-card:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-card-media { aspect-ratio: 4 / 3; background: #ece9e4; display: grid; place-items: center; } .ds-disc { width: 96px; height: 96px; border-radius: 50%; background: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.7); display: grid; place-items: center; color: var(--lost, #92400e); transition: transform 0.45s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-card:hover .ds-disc { transform: scale(1.06) rotate(-4deg); } .ds-card-body { padding: 12px 14px 16px; } .ds-card-tag { display: inline-block; font-size: 0.72rem; font-weight: 700; letter-spacing: 0.04em; padding: 2px 8px; border-radius: 4px; border: 1px solid #fcd34d; background: var(--lost-tint, #fef3c7); color: var(--lost, #92400e); } .ds-card h3 { margin: 8px 0 6px; font-family: var(--font-display, 'Bricolage Grotesque Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 1.12rem; font-weight: 680; letter-spacing: -0.01em; line-height: 1.12; color: var(--ink, #0f172a); transition: color 0.2s ease; } .ds-card:hover h3 { color: var(--primary, #1e3a6e); } .ds-meta { margin: 0 0 2px; font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--muted, #556173); }

components.css: .ds-toast { position: relative; overflow: hidden; display: grid; grid-template-columns: auto 1fr auto; gap: 10px; align-items: start; width: 360px; padding: 12px 12px 14px 14px; background: #fff; border: 1px solid var(--line, #e2e8f0); border-radius: 8px; box-shadow: 0 18px 40px -16px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.35), 0 2px 6px rgb(15 23 42 / 0.06); font-family: var(--font-body, system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-toast-icon { width: 30px; height: 30px; border-radius: 6px; display: grid; place-items: center; background: var(--found-tint, #dcfce7); color: var(--found, #166534); } .ds-toast-title { margin: 0; font-weight: 650; font-size: 0.95rem; color: var(--ink, #0f172a); } .ds-toast-msg { margin: 2px 0 0; font-size: 0.875rem; color: var(--text, #334155); } .ds-toast-close { border: 0; background: none; color: var(--muted, #556173); padding: 2px; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; display: inline-flex; } .ds-toast-close:hover { color: var(--ink, #0f172a); background: var(--soft, #f1f5f9); } .ds-toast-close:focus-visible { outline: 3px solid #93c5fd; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-toast-timer { position: absolute; left: 0; bottom: 0; height: 3px; width: 60%; background: var(--found-accent, #16a34a); opacity: 0.18; }

narrative.overview:
The system is the campus office counter made into a website: a calm, orderly navy desk where every item is logged, tagged lost or found, and handed back in person. Surfaces are white index cards and panels laid on a warm off-white ground, held together by thin slate hairlines and soft one-pixel shadows. Colour carries meaning before it carries mood: navy is the service itself, brown-orange is something missing, green is something waiting to go home. The one dark room is the home hero, where slow cyan-to-blue light beams drift behind the opening question.

Density is practical rather than airy. Pages are used between classes on a phone and at a staff counter on desktop, so lists, tables and forms stay compact and scannable, with generous space reserved for the hero and the home journey. Motion is advanced but purposeful: things come into focus, lists arrive once, a card opens into its own detail page, and the journey beam fills from lost to found as you scroll. Every motion has a reduced-motion path, and none of it carries information.

The owner has rejected purple gradients, pill-shaped buttons, emoji icons, fabricated metrics or reviews, vague hero text, placeholder content and AI-generated stock photography. These are binding.
keyCharacteristics: Navy primary, brown-orange for lost, green for found; the pair is the brand's story.
Warm off-white page ground with a faint animated navy hairline pattern behind all content.
White cards and panels with slate hairline borders and a near-invisible resting shadow.
Bricolage Grotesque for headings and numerals, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything read.
Gently squared corners (6px default); nothing is a pill.
One exponential ease-out drives nearly all motion; every effect has a reduced-motion fallback.

rules.name: The Lost Is Warm, Found Is Green Rule
rules.body: Brown-orange means lost and green means found, on every surface, every time. Neither hue is used for decoration or for any other meaning, and colour is never the only signal: the word LOST or FOUND always accompanies it.

rules.name: The No Purple Rule
rules.body: No purple anywhere, including gradients and the hero beams (which stay in the cyan-to-blue range, hue 190 to 235).

rules.name: The Two-Step Semantic Rule
rules.body: Each semantic hue has a deep step for text and fills (lost, found) and a bright step for marks, borders and swatches (lost-accent, found-accent). Use the deep step whenever text sits on it or in it.

rules.name: The Display Is for Headings Rule
rules.body: Bricolage appears only on h1 to h3 and on numerals. Everything a person reads or types is Atkinson Hyperlegible Next. Small headings that act as labels (the hero listings heading) switch to the body face.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Counts, scores, table cells and badges use tabular figures so columns of numbers do not jitter.

rules.name: The Lift on Intent Rule
rules.body: Shadows deepen only in answer to a pointer or because the layer floats. Nothing rests at Lift.

rules.name: The Soft Shadow Rule
rules.body: Every shadow is a blurred, slate-tinted ambient shadow. No hard offset shadows.

rules.name: The No Pill Rule
rules.body: Buttons and tags never take a pill or fully rounded shape. Nothing interactive exceeds 10px radius.

rules.name: The Reduced Motion Rule
rules.body: Every animation has a reduced-motion path: entrances become a 0.3s fade, hover transforms and view transitions are removed, the cursor ring, Lenis and toast timers are switched off, and canvases draw a single still frame.

dos: Do use Counter Navy for the service's own actions and Lost Umber / Found Forest only for lost and found actions and marks.
Do pair every lost or found colour with the word LOST or FOUND, or another text cue.
Do keep corners at 6px by default, 4px for small inline marks, 10px for floating sheets.
Do set headings and numerals in Bricolage Grotesque and all reading and input text in Atkinson Hyperlegible Next.
Do keep resting surfaces at the Resting shadow and reserve Lift for hover.
Do use the shared ease-out for motion and provide a reduced-motion path for every new effect.
Do show real data or nothing: hide a count or panel that cannot load rather than filling it.
Do badge any illustrative interface sample as an example, as the journey vignettes do.
Do draw icons as 24-grid stroke SVGs in currentColor, hidden from screen readers when decorative.
donts: Don't use purple, purple gradients, or beams outside the cyan-to-blue range.
Don't make pill-shaped or fully rounded buttons or tags.
Don't show fake reviews, testimonials, metrics, counters or placeholder content.
Don't use AI-generated stock photos; item photos come from reports, otherwise use the category icon disc.
Don't write vague hero text; the hero asks the user's actual question.
Don't use em dashes in interface copy.
Don't add coloured borders to cards other than the item card's 3px top edge; that edge is a deliberate exception from the owner's reference.
Don't let any decorative effect (beams, Sliding Ease, magnetic cursor) carry information.
